back: Ensure a class has exactly one instance and provide one global way to reach it.

front: Where does a Python Singleton control creation?
back: In __new__, which returns the stored instance after the first call.
__init__ runs on every construction and would reset the shared state.
Check for the instance, take the lock, check again, then create. Safe and cheap after the first call.
A module-level instance. Modules are imported once and shared through sys.modules.
A factory decorated with functools.cache. Reset it in tests with cache_clear().
Hidden global mutable state: hidden dependencies, tight coupling and tests that leak into each other.
Create one instance at startup and inject it where needed.

front: Is a Singleton one per machine?
back: No. It is one per process (and per class); worker processes each get their own.
Lazy builds on first use and needs locking. Eager builds at import and is simpler and thread-safe.
